MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 24, 2020

Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting
was conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the
City Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public
comments that were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:00 p.m., on March 24, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 19, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

  Council Member Raths

The following public comment was received via email and read by the City Clerk.

City Council Minutes  2  March 24, 2020
 Christy Bode, M.V.: wrote that it is important to have pollinators and she relies on bees for her
fruit trees and neighbor’s vegetable gardens. She feels it could be a major benefit to the community

DEPARTMENT HEAD UPDATES REGARDING COVID-19 ACTIVITIES

Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay

All essential services are still being provided throughout the City: landscape maintenance, pool
maintenance, street sweeping, trash collection, tree trimming (for safety), irrigation management
and other services needed to ensure facilities are safe. Parks and open space are still open at this
time, including public restrooms which are cleaned, wiped down and disinfected on a daily basis.
Public Services will be installing social distancing signs at the entry to each play area and kiosks
throughout parks. Hand sanitizer stations were distributed at city facilities with high foot-traffic
areas. All facilities are in the process of being deep cleaned. Disinfectant products that qualify for
use against SAS-COV-2 and COVID-19, as released by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
(EPA), are currently being used by the City. One hundred refillable 2-ounce hand sanitizer bottles
have been ordered and should arrive on Friday, March 27. Animal Services continues to provide a
full level of services, mostly through online resources and by appointment. Residents are
encouraged to refrain from using playground equipment and to use at their own risk since there is
no way to disinfect all equipment citywide. Building Services has additional facility cleaning and
disinfecting operations at each of the City’s various sites which include: restroom deep cleaning
three times per day, increased cleaning and disinfection of high-touched surfaces (i.e. door handles,
light switches, hand rails, elevator buttons, sinks and faucets, restroom stalls and dispensers,
vending machines, and countertops). Meeting and banquet room tables and chairs are being
disinfected and tagged at Norman P. Murray Community Center and the City Hall Saddleback
Room. Staff has added nightly cleaning to Orange County Sheriff Department (OCSD) office at
The Shops at Mission Viejo and all OCSD remote sites. Staff has been scheduled to work remotely
in order to continue to deliver services to the community.

Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes

Since March 14, the Emergency Operations Center (EOC) has been activated and staff continues
to monitor and report to the County EOC. The City Emergency Management Team is participating
in the County EOC’s daily conference call with the Orange County Health Care Agency. The
purpose of the call is to stay abreast of the ever-changing County and City response to the outbreak.
One of the major functions of the EOC is the dissemination of public Information. The Director
of Community Relations, along with the IT department, are helping to maintain the City’s multiple
information channels for the public. The City is also participating in daily calls including: County
Public Information Officer (PIO) conference calls, Emergency Management conference calls, and
some of the Federal conference calls which are held periodically. Since this is primarily a public
health issue, the City looks for guidance from Federal, State and County public health officials,
and in turn, communicates this guidance to the community through the City’s multiple media
outlets. City staff continue to track personnel, equipment, and supply costs for potential
reimbursement. It is anticipated that the EOC will continue to operate over the next few weeks,
depending on how the outbreak manifests in Southern California. This emergency has posed its
challenges due to social distancing guidance and limited staff but management has made the

City Council Minutes  3  March 24, 2020
 necessary adjustments and the EOC continues to operate daily in response to COVID-19. As of
1:00 p.m. today, there are 152 confirmed cases; with the number of tests conducted by the health
department and commercial labs at 2,159 tests.

Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas

The Finance, Human Resources, and Risk Management divisions have been fully functional the
past two weeks and the IT Department has provided set-up so staff can continue to perform at full
operation, whether they are working from home or at City Hall. There has been no disruption in
Administrative Services functions. Accounts Payable checks are being processed once per week
with no plans to change at this time. Contracts, purchase orders, cash receipts, payroll, and animal
licenses are continuing to be processed without exception. Employee recruitment process have had
significant changes though. Applicants for a position in the Recreation Department will be
informed that interviews may be delayed and all other recruitments have been paused and will
resume at a future date. Administrative Services staff are available to receive calls from the public,
vendors and employees between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

Director of Community Development Elaine Lister

Commercial and industrial inspections are being conducted as normal while maintaining 6-foot
social distance. Residential inspections are exterior only and Inspectors are advised to use a digital
medium to verify code compliance inside residential structures (i.e. Facetime, pictures, video etc.)
Building Inspectors have been directed not to enter City Hall. Inspection run lists and files are
placed in a secure hallway for pick-up and inspection results are entered into the permitting system
after files are returned at the end of the day and retrieved from the hallway. One Permit Technician
and one Building Inspector remain on site daily to support City Building and Safety Operations
and to facilitate inquiries and responses. The City Hall lobby hallway has been designated for plan
submittal and retrieval. Plans are placed in the hallway and after a 24-hour period they are retrieved
for processing. Once completed, applicants are advised that their plans are available for pick-up in
hallway. Inspections are down fifty percent, averaging 25-30 per day. Permitting and Plan Check
is being conducted on-line via email to bldgservices@cityofmissionviejo.org. After email contact
has been made, an applicant is given a residential or commercial information packet to fill out for
submittal and a phone number and email address are requested so Permit Technicians can
communicate with applicant. From that point, an applicant is guided through the permitting
process. The Building Department has had more than 75 email inquiries today alone.

Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman

After learning about the crisis, the Community Relations Department launched an aggressive
public information and outreach campaign. Staff established a dedicated COVID-19 web page and
it is being updated daily. Currently, more than 20 news articles have been posted about the impacts
of COVID-19 on the community. These include facility closures; health, mental and food
resources; and business news including how to support local restaurants and stimulate the
economy. Residents can find this new page at cityofmissionviejo.org/covid-19. All information
has been shared via the city’s social media sites and news media as well. Staff is responding to
questions and comments through emails, phone calls and social media. To further inform the
community, signage, fliers, posters, ad television notices regarding COVID-19 have been
provided. Creation of a video message from Mayor Goodell to the community went out last week

City Council Minutes  4  March 24, 2020
 and a second video message will be created this week. Community Relations staff are also in the
process of producing department-specific videos to inform residents of the City’s ongoing essential
services and those videos will be uploaded to social media and in a central location on the city’s
YouTube channel by week’s end. Lastly, staff digitized nearly 20 years of Storytime Theatre
episodes which will broadcast on MVTV daily at 10:30 a.m. to help parents entertain and educate
young children as they shelter in place.

Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander

As of March 13, Information Technology (I.T.) was asked to mobilize all essential city staff to
work remotely from home as each City facility was closed to the public to meet State and Local
mandates. Based on priority lists from Human Resources and department heads, ninety users have
been issued city laptops or are working from their home devices. Cyber security continues to be a
top priority and a threat for I.T. staff to continue to manage. Security briefings from the Department
of Homeland Security, FBI and other partners indicate that attack traffic has increased and phishing
emails using COVID-19 as the guise have also increased. Scams for purchasing of supplies related
to COVID-19 are also on the rise. Mission Viejo has seen an increase in attacks against its network
peaking at over 4 million per day. Security challenges have become more severe as I.T. now has
to protect not just the City systems, but also the potential for attack through staff-owned computers
that have been added through the remote work setup. At present, ninety or more users working
remotely and have access to every system that was available to them in the office. I.T. has increased
monitoring and security measures to continue to protect against cyber threats. Staff is currently
working to add an additional twenty staff members to the list to work remotely.

Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen

The Library is focusing on supporting at-home activities. No items are due and no holds will be
expiring until one week after the Library reopens. Staff is responding to phone and emails Monday
through Friday from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and there are approximately twenty patron
interactions each day via phone and email. Staff is in the process of creating online engagement
with Goodreads and will be posting recommended free resources for education and entertainment.
A Reading Challenge will be launched on social media later this week. Most Library staff are
currently working from home.

Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon

Public Works staff are working remotely for the most part and the public counter is closed. The
department recognized the importance for utility agencies to maintain and upgrade their
infrastructure and for construction projects to move forward, so permit applications continue to be
processed as normal and Inspectors remain in the field performing necessary inspections. Permits
are mostly processed electronically through the City’s website, along with a special drop-off/pick-
up area in the outer lobby at City Hall for hardcopy documents. The City’s traffic signal network
is controlled through a centralized control system that can be monitored remotely to adjust traffic
signal operations and dispatch maintenance crews as needed. Project Design also continues with
a couple of large roadway paving projects scheduled for summer and design of several future
intersection and roadway widening projects remain on track. Work with Caltrans and Orange
County Transportation Authority (OCTA) on the widening of Interstate 5 continues. Staff is

City Council Minutes  5  March 24, 2020
 responding to solid waste and recycling requests and questions along with putting the final touches
on a new solid waste agreement which will go into effect in January 2021.

Director of Recreation and Community Services Mark Nix

The Recreation and Community Services department continues to provide essential services
including: the monthly commodities program, bi-weekly Park-it Market (as a drive-through),
working with Agewell Senior Services to distribute over 700 home delivered meals to homebound
seniors, and working with Agewell to see how the City can expand the program and take on more
senior clients. The information will be marketed once details are available. In addition to
contacting the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center for assistance, the County is
promoting two resources for seniors who are self-isolating: The Office on Aging can be reached
at (800) 510-2020 and 211-Orange County at 211OC.org or dial 2-1-1. Regarding membership at
the Recreation and Tennis Centers, all accounts have been frozen and expiration dates on punch
passes and monthly passes have been extended. Members have been understanding and minimal
terminations have occurred. Staff is working on virtual activities for people to engage with while
at home including fitness programs, crafts, and fun challenges. Special events, facility rentals and
contracted classes have all been cancelled through mid-April.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  8  March 24, 2020
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum asked Director of Community Relations Karen Hamman if the City’s
website has a section on volunteer opportunities for residents. Director Hamman responded that
there is “Volunteer” tab on the website at the top of the page that links to the list of volunteer
opportunities, including those specifically for the COVID-19 crisis. The direct URL is
cityofmissionvieo.org/volunteer-opportunities. Council Member Bucknum thanked Mayor Pro
Tem Kelley for serving on the Transportation Corridor Agency along with the other Board
Members. Council Member Bucknum expressed her gratitude to City Staff for the work they are
doing in this time of crisis and she reminded residents to maintain social distancing and to stay
safe. Lastly, she sent caring thoughts out to two friends who are in the hospital.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked the Mayor for doing a great job during this crisis. He too inquired
about volunteer opportunities and Director Hamman responded that the City just published a news
article about residents supporting local medical personnel by making protective masks and gowns.
The article can be viewed at cityofmissionviejo.org/news and it will be cross-posted on the
dedicated COVID-19 webpage. Director Hamman restated that those interested in volunteering
can visit cityofmissionvieo.org/volunteer-opportunities to find out how to register their time and
resources.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs complimented staff on their reports this evening and specifically the
creativity that the Library is implementing to assist kids at home. He also commended some local
businesses such as The Broken Yolk Cafe that is feeding first responders and Smart Cups for
putting together hand sanitizers. Council Member Sachs said the community is really coming
together during this crisis.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she was happy to teleconference for the meeting during
these unprecedented times. She gave kudos to staff for the amazing job they are all doing and the
great communication and information that is being given to the residents and the City Council.
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that there is always a silver lining and what she has seen on social
media is an outpouring of kindness. She pointed out to the residents that there are early grocery
shopping hours for seniors and she encouraged people to take walks to keep their spirits up and
get fresh air. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that she has six grandchildren who are being
homeschooled during this time and she sympathizes with the challenges that parents are facing.
She noted that many churches are offering services online as well as virtual bible studies. Mayor
Pro Tem Kelley encouraged people to pray for the first responders, fire fighters, law enforcement,
hospital workers, grocery store clerks, and for America. She stated that people of faith need to
send up their prayer and she concluded by asking Mission Viejo residents to take care.

City Council Minutes  9  March 24, 2020
 Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell announced that the Skjerven Family has assembled a group of volunteers to make
plastic facial shields for hospital staff. Since Saturday, they have made 3,450 shields and they are
also creating kits for assembly. Their goal is to make 5,000 a week and they are in need of
donations of plastic, foam rubber, and nylon.

14.  Mission Viejo Nadadores Financial Relief Due to the Covid-19 Outbreak

  Mayor Goodell presented his report.

  The following public comments were received via email and read by the City Clerk.

  Rosalie De Vito, M.V.: Does not agree with any further funding from the City to the
  Nadadores. She feels that the City has subsidized them with taxpayer money for too long.

  Barry Draskovich, M.V.: Recommended that the Council reject financial relief to the
  Nadadores. He stated that the Nadadores are well funded and have a healthy balance sheet.

  Kristin Yellin, M.V.: Wrote that it is a prudent decision to provide financial relief to the
  Nadadores to keep the facility in good working condition.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed opposition to the Nadadores using Council connections
  and said that their finances are not a taxpayer problem to resolve. She shared various
  financial statistics on the Nadadores program and expressed concern that the City’s
  reserves are at an all-time low due to the purchase of the golf course.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum to (1)
  approve that the City provide a month to month fee waiver of this payment at a rate of
  $6,523.33/month for annual allocation of utility expenses. This waiver would end upon use
  restrictions being lifted by the California Department of Health and the Orange County
  Public Health Agency; (2) approve that the City provide a month to month financial
  assistance of these contracted service payments at a rate of $4,250.00/month for pool and
  janitorial maintenance (the contracts would remain with the Nadadores Foundation and the
  City would reimburse the cost of these contracted payments to the Nadadores
  organization.) This financial assistance would end upon use restrictions being lifted by the
  California Department of Health and the Orange County Public Health Agency; and (3)
  approve that the City provide a 3-month deferment of this payment at a rate of
  $6,608.20/month for a total deferment of $19,824.60 for the Funding Agreement. The
  deferral amount would be added to the end of the 240- month term. The revised length of
  the loan- term would be 243 months.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  *Mayor Goodell recused himself from voting.
